diagnoses.description: security_config_generator’s JWT output is not self-contained/compilable: it generates a SecurityConfig that references JwtAuthenticationFilter (and an AuthService in AuthController) but does not generate those required classes, so the produced configuration set is incomplete and will not build as-is.

locations.section: generate_jwt_config(): generated SecurityConfig.java references JwtAuthenticationFilter/JwtAuthenticationEntryPoint; generated AuthController.java references AuthService; missing corresponding generated classes

diagnoses.description: performance_profiler’s EntityGraph check is logically incorrect and will almost never trigger: it looks for @OneToMany/@ManyToMany annotations inside repository interfaces (where they don’t exist—those are on entity classes), then returns early, causing false negatives for repositories that should be flagged for missing @EntityGraph usage.

locations.section: QueryAnalyzer._check_entity_graph(): checks '@OneToMany'/'@ManyToMany' in repository content and returns early

diagnoses.description: jackson-security guidance overstates that empty-key ("") presence is inherently undiscoverable post-deserialization; in common Jackson patterns (e.g., Map-backed DTOs or @JsonAnySetter), the empty key can remain observable in the resulting object and can be validated post-deserialization, so the document’s blanket claim is misleading.

locations.section: “The Empty Key (\"\") Attack Vector” → “The Visibility Problem” (claims there is no standard way to know an empty key was present)
